name: together-shared-workspace-journey
description: Machine-readable twin of EVALS.md: the expected tool journeys on /together, the refusal an agent must get at each gate, and the invariants every run has to hold. Verified by hand against the live page; see EVALS.md for dates and results.

would_refuse.message_operator: no_reply_address (until the human saves an email)

phases.state: valid draft at rev N, approval.state = none

phases.note: Any draft_task call bumps the rev and withdraws the open request.
submit_approved_task consumes the approval; a second call refuses with not_approved.
Delivery is locked to the human's own email or status polling; an agent-set contact_email is ignored. The grant retires itself at expiry or when the budget is spent.

journeys.human_says: Work with me on this page — read my goal and draft the task for my approval.
journeys.expected_outcome: Draft appears field by field with agent provenance; approval bar shows the exact rev; await_human blocks until the click.

journeys.human_says: Actually, make it a one-day deadline.
journeys.expected_outcome: Old request withdrawn automatically; new request binds to the new rev.
Submits the shared draft exactly as approved; task card appears; approval consumed.
Live status including seen_by_operator_at; unknown IDs return task_not_found and never a fake card.

journeys.human_says: Ask the operator whether photos are possible first.
journeys.expected_outcome: One thread per workspace; the reply lands on the page and at the human's email.

journeys.human_says: I turned Autopilot on — go ahead.
journeys.expected_outcome: No approval round-trip; budget decremented; delivery locked to the human's email.

journeys.human_says: (agent tries to submit an unapproved or edited draft)
journeys.expected_outcome: Structured refusal: not_approved, invalid_draft, or already_submitted, with the reason.

invariants.truncation_policy: longest text fields shortened with a marker; structure never dropped; a `truncated` note lists the fields
invariants.enforcement_boundary: client-side; server-verifiable approval proofs are future work and are not claimed
